title: Modi and Merz Say India-EU Trade Deal Will Unlock New Opportunities
excerpt: In a phone call marking 75 years of India-Germany ties, the two leaders pointed to the concluded India-EU free trade agreement — expected to be signed in December — as the next driver of trade, investment, defence and technology cooperation.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi received a telephone call from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Tuesday, and the two leaders reviewed the India-Germany Strategic Partnership as the countries mark 75 years of diplomatic relations.
  • Modi and Merz noted that the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement would unlock new opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and investment, and discussed cooperation in defence and advanced technologies.
  • The free trade agreement, whose negotiations concluded in January, is expected to be signed in December; more than 99 percent of Indian exports by trade value are set to gain preferential access to the EU market.
  • For Indian professionals, the pact includes a mobility framework covering intra-corporate transferees, contractual service suppliers and independent professionals across several sectors.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Tuesday that the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement would unlock new opportunities for expanding trade and investment, as the two leaders reviewed the India-Germany Strategic Partnership in a telephone call.

Modi received the call from Merz, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office. The leaders expressed satisfaction at the sustained momentum in bilateral engagements and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation across key sectors, including defence and advanced technologies, as India and Germany celebrate 75 years of diplomatic relations this year.

They also exchanged views on regional and global developments, agreed to work closely together to promote global peace, stability and a rules-based international order, and emphasised the importance of continued cooperation at multilateral fora, the statement said.

"Trade in services reached $83.10 billion in 2024."

A deal concluded in January, awaiting signature

The call comes ahead of the expected signing of the India-EU free trade agreement in December. India and the 27-member European Union concluded negotiations on the pact on January 27, when Modi and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen jointly announced the conclusion at the 16th India-EU Summit in New Delhi, ending talks that were relaunched in 2022 after years of stalemate.

An Indian official told news agency ANI that the agreement is likely to be signed during Modi's December visit to Europe, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said this week that India was hopeful of signing in December 2026, and said separately at a FICCI panel that India was aiming to operationalise the agreement in the first quarter of 2027.

What the agreement contains

According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, more than 99 percent of Indian exports by trade value will gain preferential entry into the EU, and tariffs on nearly $33 billion of exports in labour-intensive sectors — textiles, leather, marine products, gems and jewellery among them — are expected to fall to zero when the agreement enters into force. India has safeguarded sensitive agricultural products and the dairy sector, which get no market-access commitments, and agreed to a carefully calibrated liberalisation for automobiles with reciprocal access.

Beyond goods, the pact covers services, digital trade, customs and trade facilitation, and intellectual property. Its mobility framework is the element most directly relevant to the Indian diaspora in Europe: it sets out commitments for the movement of skilled and semi-skilled Indian professionals, including intra-corporate transferees, contractual service suppliers and independent professionals across several sectors.

The scale of the relationship explains the push. Bilateral trade in goods between India and the EU stood at Rs 11.5 lakh crore ($136.54 billion) in 2024-25, with Indian exports worth $75.85 billion and imports of $60.68 billion, according to the Commerce Ministry. Trade in services reached $83.10 billion in 2024.

What happens next

The December signing, if it proceeds as officials expect, would be followed by the legal formalities on both sides before the agreement enters into force; India's stated aim is to operationalise it in the first quarter of 2027. For exporters in the labour-intensive sectors named in the pact, and for Indian professionals whose mobility the framework addresses, the entry-into-force date — not the signing — is when the new terms begin to apply.
